name: The Age of AI
tagline: Real people. AI host. The age we're all living through.
description: The Age of AI is the Nerra Network's interview show with the roles reversed: an AI host, real human guests, live recorded conversations, and disclosure built into every episode. An honest chronicle of the AI age, one conversation at a time.

episodes.title: Ep8: Sameer Ranjan — A mining engineer turned AI builder weighs how platforms guiding career choice and soft skills can keep human judgment central when the models risk automating the decisions they claim to augment.
episodes.summary: Sameer Ranjan, a mining engineer turned AI builder, described how his platform normalizes personality and soft-skill scores inside separate cultural baselines instead of forcing a single universal scale. episodes.summary: Matt Davis described the most surprising effect of embedding AI agents in enterprise software delivery as the way senior judgment scales across many programs at once, while human decision points remain fixed at key gates. episodes.title: Ep5: John Capobianco — A network automation builder who turned early ChatGPT experiments into a production-grade ReAct agent now weighs how much human oversight and orchestration remain essential once agents handle intent, verification, and collaboration in regulated environments.
episodes.summary: John Capobianco revealed that his production ReAct agent can now parse high-level intent, verify proposed changes against live network state, and coordinate with peer agents before any human sees the plan, yet he still routes every change through mandatory approval gates in regulated environments.
